pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, 48-week study (Study 408-C-1402 Part 2, MOXIe)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in modified Friedreich's Ataxia Rating Scale (mFARS) score at Week 48
pivotal_trials.result: In the pre-specified Full Analysis Set (patients without pes cavus, n=82): LS mean difference -2.41 points favoring omaveloxolone (p=0.0138); omaveloxolone mean change -1.56 points (improvement), placebo mean change +0.85 points (worsening). In All Randomized Population (n=103): LS mean difference -1.94 points (nominal p=0.0331). Key secondary endpoints PGIC and CGIC did not reach statistical significance in FAS (p=0.1300 and p=0.5259); ADL nominally significant (p=0.04).

pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, long-term extension of Study 408-C-1402; post-hoc propensity score-matched analysis vs. FA-COMS natural history cohort (NCT0309078)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in mFARS at Year 3 (Study 1402 Extension vs. propensity-matched FA-COMS natural history patients)
pivotal_trials.result: Pooled population (Match 1, n=136): LS mean difference -3.354 points favoring omaveloxolone at Year 3 (p=0.0002); FA-COMS progressed 6.337 mFARS points vs. omaveloxolone-treated 2.983 points. Placebo-to-omaveloxolone (Match 2): difference -4.096 points (p=0.0001). Omaveloxolone-to-omaveloxolone (Match 3): difference -4.240 points (p=0.0190).

key_safety: In the placebo-controlled study (n=51 omaveloxolone), the most common adverse events (≥20%) were elevated liver enzymes (37.3% vs. 1.9% placebo), headache (37.3%), nausea (33.3%), abdominal pain (29.4%), skin abrasion (25.5%), and fatigue (23.5%); ALT ≥3×ULN occurred in 31.4% of omaveloxolone patients (vs. 0% placebo), and increases in BNP, NT-proBNP, cholesterol, and LDL-C were observed without cases of Hy's law or jaundice.
target_moa: Activation of the transcription factor nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2), which restores mitochondrial function, reduces oxidative stress, and reduces neuroinflammation

_meta.indication: SKYCLARYS is indicated for the treatment of Friedreich's ataxia in adults and adolescents aged 16 years and older.

indication_details.population_restrictions: adults and adolescents aged 16 years and older

supplements.description: Updated labeling only — no new indication, population, dose, or use was approved; changes reflect completed postmarketing study results (QTc safety data, CYP3A4 inducer drug interaction clarification, renal impairment PK data, carcinogenicity findings), minor dosing instruction clarification ("or 2 hours after eating"), addition of postmarketing hypersensitivity reactions, and pregnancy registry information.
